title: Coach houses, stable fittings and service wings for the Prairie Avenue 1904 programme (package K12, the kit)
status: Declared and generated, not yet built to. No lot in the scene carries this kit today; T-2321 puts the first K12 coach house or service wing on a named Prairie Avenue lot from this file and this generator.
rule: A service building is closed on every side and every part of it stands on something. Every wall is a solid with its openings cut THROUGH it (a reveal on all sides, never a dark rectangle painted on a face); a wall that meets another wall, a roof or the ground leaves its open edges lying on that surface, so there is no gap and no face laid on a face; a fixing (a hinge, a hoist beam, a coping, a ramp cleat) is a closed piece passing through what carries it. A ramp and a stair meet grade at their foot and the floor or landing they serve at their head. The parts' sizes are data here and the generator reads them; the check (tools/check_coach_house_kit.py) rebuilds every variant and holds the built geometry to this file.
frame: Each variant is authored about its own `base` socket (k01_contract.json component_frame): the centre of its alley wall at grade on the wall's outer face, +X along that wall, +Y up, +Z out of it into the alley. The building runs back from the alley along -Z.

restrictions.why: ASSET-CATALOG.md section K12: '1911 garage/auto labels are not 1904 use evidence.' The kit builds a horse-drawn coach house (carriage bay, loft hatch and hoist, stable sash, a ramp to a stable basement). A named target that is labelled a garage or an auto house on the 1911 Sanborn is not thereby a garage in 1904, and none of these parts is a motor-garage part.

ASSET-CATALOG.md section K12: 'roof ventilator only when supported.' A variant may ask for a ridge ventilator only with a source that shows one on its building; without one the generator refuses it, and the kit itself carries none.

Every size and form here is generic. A lot whose own coach house is documented (Glessner's stable is the scene's one, and it is its own canonical asset) is built from that evidence, never from this kit.

parts._doc: The working sizes every variant starts from, in metres. Wall-local positions are (s, y, n): s along the wall from its start, y up from grade, n out of its outer face (a wall occupies -thickness..0).

wall.note: A 13-inch (three-brick) wall for the two-storey coach house and its party wall, a 9-inch (two-brick) wall for the one-storey lean-to and connecting wing: the common Chicago load-bearing sizes for buildings of these heights.

storeys.note: A carriage room tall enough for a closed carriage with a coachman's seat (3.6 m to the loft floor) and a loft or coachman's quarters over it (2.7 m to the eave).

basement.note: A stable basement floor 1.8 m under grade, reached by the ramp. The foundation walls go down to it all round.

roof.note: A plain gable roof over the coach house, ridge parallel to the alley: rafters, boards and covering as one 0.25 m slab, 0.4 m eaves, a 0.3 m verge at the open gable. Coverings, gutters and flashing are K04's; the shell is K05's to replace when the kit is put on a house.

party_wall.note: A party (fire) wall on the lot line: it rises 0.45 m above the roof's surface along the whole rake, and returns 0.5 m past both eaves so the roof dies into it rather than running past its end. Capped by a weathered stone coping 0.43 m wide (50 mm over each face) let 30 mm into the wall.

opening.note: Door and hatch leaves are 60 mm boarded leaves set 0.10 m back from the face, a pair meeting on a 10 mm gap. A window has a stone sill running 0.08 m past each jamb, 0.10 m deep and 50 mm proud; a flat head has a stone lintel 0.10 m past each jamb, 0.20 m high and 30 mm proud.

carriage.note: The carriage bay: a clear opening of 2.7-3.6 m (a carriage and pair turning in from an alley), under a segmental brick head two rowlocks deep (0.23 m) standing 20 mm proud, closed by a pair of boarded leaves on three strap hinges each and a boarded head panel filling the segment.

hoist.note: A timber hoist beam over the loft hatch, 0.9 m out from the wall and let 0.25 m into it, with an iron hook near its end: how hay and feed went up into the loft.

sash.note: A plain stable sash: a 60 mm frame set 0.10 m back, divided into four lights by a meeting rail and a muntin, glazed with one pane per light.

ramp.note: A straight ramp down to the stable basement: at most 1 in 4 (horses were led down steeper ramps than people walk, on cleats), 1.3 m between two 0.3 m retaining walls that stand 0.15 m above grade as a curb, a 1.4 m level landing at the basement door, and a cleat across it every 0.45 m.

stair.note: An external timber service stair up to a loft door: housed stringers 0.28 m deep, 40 mm treads with a 20 mm nosing, risers of at most 0.21 m and goings of at least 0.22 m, a 1.2 m landing on two posts and a 0.9 m handrail from a newel at its foot.

lean_to.note: A one-storey lean-to against the coach house's yard wall, its single-pitch roof dying into that wall: a feed or harness room, with a stable (Dutch) door in two leaves.

wing.note: A one-storey connecting wing from the coach house to the house, flat-roofed, its walls and roof dying into the coach house at one end and the house's rear wall at the other: the kit's 'connecting wing' and the 'believable workyard connection' K12 asks for.

ventilator.note: No ridge ventilator. The asset catalog allows one only where a source shows it; this kit has no such source, so it builds none and the generator refuses a variant that asks for one without evidence.

costs._doc: Triangle budget per variant, as built, without its board. A variant over its budget is refused, so a kit change that bloats every alley in the town is caught here.

_variants_doc: kind picks the builder; class picks the triangle budget. width_m runs along the alley (party wall included), depth_m back from it. Openings are on a wall (alley, yard, gable, lean_to, wing_east, wing_west), at s0..s1 along it from its start, sill to head in metres from grade; a carriage opening's head is its springing line.

variants.note: A two-storey brick coach house on an alley, the kind the 1904 Prairie Avenue lots kept behind their houses: a carriage bay with paired leaves under a segmental head, a man door, stable sash, a loft hatch with its hoist beam, a party wall on the lot line, an external stair to a loft door on the open gable, a cleated ramp down to a stable basement on the yard side, a lean-to with a stable door, and a connecting wing to the house.
